title: Telang's edition of Bhartṛhari's śatakas (Digital Library of India scan)
description: The scan of the Digital Library of India begins and ends with the library's cover, labels and barcode pages. The book has an English preface and introduction with footnotes; a critical notice describing the sources; addenda et corrigenda; an index of stanzas in tables printed sideways; the Sanskrit text of the Nītiśataka and the Vairāgyaśataka, in sections, with a critical apparatus of variant readings below a rule on each page; and English notes on the stanzas.

flows.main: The parts of the book in reading order.
flows.apparatus: The variant readings, in page order.
flows.notes: The footnotes of the English parts and the notes below the index tables, in page order.

introduction.description: The English preface and introduction, with page numbers in roman numerals.

critical_notice.description: The critical notice after the introduction, headed CRITICAL NOTICE., describing the printed editions and manuscripts used and their sigla.

corrigenda.description: The pages headed ADDENDA ET CORRIGENDA., a list of corrections, with short lines introducing groups of them, such as In Index No. I. the following corrections should be made.

index.description: The index of stanzas: tables giving each stanza's number in other editions and manuscripts, with the headings INDEX. and INDEX No. 2.

shataka.description: The Sanskrit text of one śataka, with its title and sections, ending with its miscellaneous stanzas: one unit from its title to the next śataka or the notes, going on across the heading MISCELLANEOUS.

section.description: A group of stanzas on one theme, with its heading, such as अथ दुर्जनप्रशंसा ।. The miscellaneous stanzas at the end of a śataka, headed MISCELLANEOUS., are its last section: the śataka goes on across that heading.

notes.description: The English notes on the stanzas, after the text: one unit for the notes on both śatakas and their miscellaneous stanzas. Its headings, such as NOTES., MISCELLANEOUS., VAIRĀGYAS'ATAKA. and MISCELLANEOUS STANZAS., are inside it, and it goes on across them.

heading.description: A title or heading: of a part, of a śataka, or of a section, such as अथ दुर्जनप्रशंसा ।

paragraph.description: A paragraph of the English preface, introduction or critical notice, such as one describing an edition, C. The Bombay Oblong edition, …; or a line introducing corrections in the addenda et corrigenda.

corrigendum.description: One correction of the addenda et corrigenda, such as P. 6. (Text) line 1 from bottom, for … read …, with its page reference.

table.description: One index table, with its column heads (the sigla of editions and manuscripts) and, in each row, the first words of a stanza and its numbers. The tables are printed sideways; the page images of the index have been turned upright.

lead_in.description: A short Sanskrit line of its own that introduces the next stanza, such as साहंकारं पुरुषमुद्दिश्याह ।

verse.description: One Sanskrit stanza with its number in Devanagari digits, such as ॥ २९ ॥. Its lines are set alternately flush and indented. A stanza can begin at the foot of one page and end at the top of the next.

apparatus_entry.description: The variant readings of one stanza, below the rule: the stanza's Roman numeral, such as XXVIII., then readings for its quarters (a) to (d) with the sigla of the sources, such as K. Bo. M. An entry can run onto the next page; the apparatus at the top of that page then continues it without a numeral, for example from (c).

stanza_note.description: The English note on one stanza, beginning with its number, such as St. XXXIII.—, and often ending with the name of the metre, such as —Anushṭubh. A note can run across pages.

footnote.description: A footnote below the rule in the preface, introduction, critical notice or notes, marked *, †, ‡, §, ¶ or ‖; or a note printed below an index table, such as N. B.—The numbers marked * refer to the Miscellaneous Stanzas….

page_number.description: The page number at the head of the page: Devanagari digits in brackets on text pages, such as [ ७२ ]; roman numerals in the introduction; Arabic digits in the notes.

running_header.description: The running title beside the page number, such as NOTES.

scan_matter.description: Matter of the scan, not of the book: the library's covers and labels (NOT TO BE ISSUED OUT OF THE LIBRARY.), stamps, barcodes and accession numbers, and the note Digitized with financial assistance from the Government of Maharashtra.

relations.note: A footnote marker in the text points to its footnote.
relations.readings: An apparatus entry gives the readings of the stanza with the same number.
relations.comments_on: A stanza note comments on the stanza with the same number.

conventions: Transcribe Devanagari and English as printed, in Unicode NFC, with the printed digits and dandas. Keep the edition's romanization in the English, such as S'ringâras'ataka and Kâvyasangraha, and the degree signs (°) that mark abbreviated readings in the apparatus.
In a table, transcribe each printed row as one line, with the cells separated by ' | ' and a cell that has only dots written as ..

source.revision: 2026-11-06: Claude's additions for the Telang full-book walk, not yet reviewed by the user: critical_notice and corrigenda with corrigendum; scan_matter furniture; footnote, paragraph, table and index descriptions widened to the whole scan; the table convention. The list the user accepted had sha256 b408c43875e6dfbcac3646350df894194311b9219e349ccc6cd1e3649bc87d55 and is saved as type-list.json with every earlier Telang result. Revised the same day after the transcription pilot: paragraph allowed in corrigenda (page 34's introductory line); the seven other pilot pages were transcribed with the list before this change, which affects only the corrigenda. Revised again after pages 1-120 had been transcribed: the section description says that the miscellaneous stanzas are the last section of their śataka (page 118 had begun a new śataka at MISCELLANEOUS.). Revised a third time after the whole book had been transcribed: the shataka and notes descriptions say each goes on across its internal headings (pages 118 and 161 had begun new top-level units there); pages 118 and 161 were transcribed again.
